what_its_for: Demeclocycline is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including respiratory tract infections, urinary tract infections, skin infections, and some sexually transmitted infections. It is also sometimes used to treat a condition called SIADH (syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone), which causes your body to hold too much water.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, usually 2 to 4 times a day as directed by your doctor. Take it on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals, because food and dairy products (like milk, cheese, or yogurt) can reduce how well this medicine works. Swallow the tablet or capsule whole with a full glass of water (8 ounces). Do not lie down for at least 30 minutes after taking it to help prevent stomach irritation. Always finish your full course of antibiotics even if you feel better early.
dosing: For most infections, the usual adult dose is 150 mg taken 4 times a day, or 300 mg taken 2 times a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on the type and severity of your infection. For SIADH, doses are typically higher, around 600 to 1200 mg per day in divided doses. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store demeclocycline at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children. Important: Do NOT use this medication after its expiration date. Expired tetracycline-type antibiotics like demeclocycline can be harmful to your kidneys.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids, calcium supplements, iron supplements, magnesium-containing laxatives, or dairy products within 2 hours of taking this medicine, as they can prevent it from working properly. Avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight or tanning beds because demeclocycline can make your skin much more sensitive to the sun and increase your risk of a serious sunburn. Wear sunscreen and protective clothing when going outdoors. Avoid taking this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without talking to your doctor first. Do not give demeclocycline to children under 8 years old unless specifically directed by a doctor, as it can permanently stain developing teeth.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: severe sunburn or unusual skin reaction after sun exposure, severe or watery diarrhea (which could be a sign of a serious bowel infection), signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain, signs of kidney problems such as decreased urination or swelling in your legs or feet, severe headache or blurred vision, difficulty swallowing or severe throat pain, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing, or unusual increased thirst and urination (especially when used for SIADH).
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting demeclocycline, but it is very important to keep taking all of your doses as prescribed even if your symptoms improve. Stopping too early can allow bacteria to grow back and make your infection harder to treat. For SIADH, it may take several days to see improvement in your sodium or fluid balance levels.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Demeclocycline should NOT be used during pregnancy, especially during the second and third trimester, as it can harm the developing baby's bones and teeth. It also passes into breast milk and can harm a nursing baby, so breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medicine. Children: This medicine should NOT be given to children under 8 years old because it can permanently stain teeth yellow-gray-brown and affect bone development. Kidney or Liver Disease: If you have kidney or liver problems, tell your doctor before starting this medicine. Your dose may need to be adjusted, and you may need closer monitoring. Elderly Patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine and should use it with caution.
